I think this is a great direction. Small suggestions:

_Verify that all HTTP responses include the X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header to prevent content and MIME type and sniffing, require that resources declare a correct and expected Content-Type header (e.g., stylesheets must use text/css), and ensure that Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB) is enabled._

So I really struggled with this and I think @elarlang's suggestion made things a lot clearer to me, even though it is a little wordier. The think about request destinations is really subtle and not something  I was aware of.

Some subtle changes:

_"Verify that all HTTP responses contain an 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' header field. This instructs browsers not to use content sniffing and MIME type guessing for the given response, and to require the response's Content-Type header field value to match the destination resource. For example, the response to a request for a style is only accepted if the response's Content-Type is 'text/css'. This also enables the use of the Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB) header field which the response should also contain._"

This is not a header field, it's a browser's feature.

Just update to my previous proposal to explain the point:
> Verify that all HTTP responses contain an 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' header field. This instructs browsers not to use content sniffing and MIME type guessing for the given response, instructs to require a correct Content-Type header field value from the destination resource (such as a resource for style is accepted only with text/css), and **enables browsers' Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB) functionality**.

> This also enables the use of the Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB) header field which the response should also contain.

This is not a header field, it's a browser's feature.
